{"parentUuid":"bc9e0e0d-622f-4ee4-8562-fbcc0ca75b06","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"41d96f36-c558-41bc-8e41-725cff6d0f28","agentId":"a86563067579899f5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01KcaxeNhRJYjqb7GZuzDxLm","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"SIGIL MCP memory server (Phase 0a: memory.search).\n2\t\n3\tA gated, read-only, loopback stdio server exposing the owner's total recall to any Claude\n4\tsurface. Ports the CRUCIBLE MCP posture (framework/v2/mcp/server.py): a fail-closed tool\n5\tallowlist, no write path, and provenance on every result — each hit is a real, tamper-\n6\tevident spine record (seq + entry_hash) so answers are CITED, and an empty result says so\n7\trather than inviting fabrication (SIGIL doctrine §1.5, prove-don't-guess).\n8\t\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\tfrom typing import Any\n12\t\n13\tfrom mcp.server.fastmcp import FastMCP\n14\t\n15\tfrom ..config import EMBED_MODEL, QDRANT_URL\n16\tfrom ..reuse import assert_no_offense\n17\tfrom ..spine.checkpoint import verify_checkpoint\n18\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n19\tfrom ..vectors.index import VectorIndex\n20\t\n21\tassert_no_offense()  # doctrine §12: no engine module may be loaded in a SIGIL process\n22\t\n23\tmcp = FastMCP(\"sigil-memory\")\n24\t_index: VectorIndex | None = None\n25\t\n26\t\n27\tdef _idx() -> VectorIndex:\n28\t    global _index\n29\t    if _index is None:\n30\t        _index = VectorIndex()\n31\t    return _index\n32\t\n33\t\n34\t@mcp.tool()\n35\tdef memory_search(query: str, k: int = 8) -> dict[str, Any]:\n36\t    \"\"\"Search the owner's ENTIRE Claude history — everything they've built, decided, or\n37\t    discussed — and return ranked memory records WITH PROVENANCE so you can cite them.\n38\t\n39\t    Each result is a real, tamper-evident spine record: `seq` + `entry_hash` uniquely\n40\t    identify it, `when`/`session`/`project` locate it. When you answer from these, CITE\n41\t    the seq(s). If `results` is empty, memory genuinely has nothing — say so; do NOT\n42\t    fabricate an answer.\n43\t\n44\t    Args:\n45\t        query: what to recall (natural language).\n46\t        k: max results (default 8).\n47\t    \"\"\"\n48\t    hits, is_grounded = _idx().grounded(query, k=max(1, min(int(k), 25)))\n49\t    if not is_grounded:\n50\t        return {\"results\": [],\n51\t                \"note\": \"No strongly-grounded match in SIGIL memory for this query. Do not fabricate — \"\n52\t                        \"tell the owner memory has nothing solid on this (optionally suggest rephrasing).\"}\n53\t    return {\n54\t        \"results\": [\n55\t            {\n56\t                \"seq\": h[\"seq\"], \"kind\": h[\"kind\"], \"when\": h.get(\"ts\"),\n57\t                \"session\": h.get(\"session_id\"), \"project\": h.get(\"project\"),\n58\t                \"entry_hash\": h.get(\"entry_hash\"), \"score\": round(h[\"score\"], 4),\n59\t                \"text\": h.get(\"text\"),\n60\t            }\n61\t            for h in hits\n62\t        ],\n63\t        \"provenance\": \"Each result is a tamper-evident spine record; cite its `seq` (and `entry_hash`) when you answer.\",\n64\t    }\n65\t\n66\t\n67\t@mcp.tool()\n68\tdef episodic_range(start_seq: int = 0, end_seq: int | None = None,\n69\t                   kind: str | None = None, limit: int = 25) -> dict[str, Any]:\n70\t    \"\"\"Read a CONTIGUOUS window of the owner's episodic spine in seq order — the raw record\n71\t    stream (messages, tool calls, commits, docs), not a semantic search. Use this to\n72\t    reconstruct *what happened* around a known point (e.g. after `memory_search` gives you a\n73\t    seq, read the seqs around it for context), or to page through a session/day.\n74\t\n75\t    Every record is tamper-evident (seq + entry_hash). Cite seqs when you answer.\n76\t\n77\t    Args:\n78\t        start_seq: first seq to return (inclusive, default 0 = beginning).\n79\t        end_seq: last seq (inclusive); default = newest.\n80\t        kind: optional filter (message | tool_call | tool_result | commit | document | session | decision | commitment | brief).\n81\t        limit: max records (default 25, hard cap 200).\n82\t    \"\"\"\n83\t    store = SpineStore()\n84\t    limit = max(1, min(int(limit), 200))\n85\t    hi = (store.next_seq - 1) if end_seq is None else int(end_seq)\n86\t    lo = max(0, int(start_seq))\n87\t    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n88\t    for r in store.iter_records(since_seq=lo - 1):  # yields seq >= lo\n89\t        if r.seq > hi:\n90\t            break\n91\t        if kind and r.kind != kind:\n92\t            continue\n93\t        out.append({\n94\t            \"seq\": r.seq, \"kind\": r.kind, \"source\": r.source, \"actor\": r.actor,\n95\t            \"when\": r.ts, \"session\": r.payload.get(\"session_id\"), \"project\": r.payload.get(\"project\"),\n96\t            \"parent_id\": r.parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": r.supersedes_id,\n97\t            \"entry_hash\": r.entry_hash, \"text\": (r.text() or \"\")[:800],\n98\t        })\n99\t        if len(out) >= limit:\n100\t            break\n101\t    return {\"range\": {\"start_seq\": lo, \"end_seq\": hi}, \"kind\": kind, \"count\": len(out),\n102\t            \"records\": out,\n103\t            \"provenance\": \"Each record is a tamper-evident spine entry; cite its `seq` when you answer.\"}\n104\t\n105\t\n106\t@mcp.tool()\n107\tdef ingest_status(verify: bool = True) -> dict[str, Any]:\n108\t    \"\"\"Report the health of SIGIL memory: how much is stored, how much is embedded for\n109\t    semantic recall, and — with `verify` — whether the spine's integrity chain and signed\n110\t    head still hold (tamper-evidence). Use this to tell the owner how current/trustworthy\n111\t    their memory is before relying on it.\n112\t\n113\t    Args:\n114\t        verify: also run the (heavier) integrity + signed-head check (default true).\n115\t    \"\"\"\n116\t    store = SpineStore()\n117\t    vi = _idx()\n118\t    status: dict[str, Any] = {\n119\t        \"spine_records\": store.count(),\n120\t        \"next_seq\": store.next_seq,\n121\t        \"vectors_indexed\": vi.count(),\n122\t        \"last_indexed_seq\": vi.last_indexed_seq(),\n123\t        \"embedding_model\": EMBED_MODEL,\n124\t        \"qdrant_mode\": \"server\" if QDRANT_URL else \"local-embedded\",\n125\t    }\n126\t    if verify:\n127\t        ok, msg = store.verify()\n128\t        hok, hmsg = verify_checkpoint(store)\n129\t        status[\"chain\"] = {\"ok\": ok, \"detail\": msg}\n130\t        status[\"signed_head\"] = {\"ok\": hok, \"detail\": hmsg}\n131\t    return status\n132\t\n133\t\n134\t@mcp.tool()\n135\tdef graph_entity(name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n136\t    \"\"\"Look up a structural entity in the owner's memory graph and return it WITH its\n137\t    neighbours and spine anchors. Resolves `name` as a Project, then a Session id, a Commit\n138\t    hash prefix, or a Document path substring. Use this for a structured overview — e.g.\n139\t    `graph_entity(\"PENTEST-main\")` returns the project's sessions, commits, and documents.\n140\t\n141\t    The graph is a deterministic, rebuilt view of the spine; every node cites the spine\n142\t    `anchor_seq` that minted it, so you can `episodic_range` around it for detail.\n143\t    \"\"\"\n144\t    from ..graph import entity as _entity\n145\t    try:\n146\t        return _entity(name)\n147\t    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001 — graph may be unbuilt; report, don't crash the tool\n148\t        return {\"error\": str(e), \"hint\": \"the graph may not be built yet\"}\n149\t\n150\t\n151\t@mcp.tool()\n152\tdef graph_query(cypher: str, limit: int = 50) -> dict[str, Any]:\n153\t    \"\"\"Run a READ-ONLY Cypher query over the owner's memory graph (a deterministic view of\n154\t    the spine) and return columns + rows. Writes/DDL are refused.\n155\t\n156\t    Node labels: `Project(name, sessions, commits, documents, messages)`,\n157\t    `Session(id, title, project, messages, first_seq, last_seq, anchor_seq)`,\n158\t    `Document(path, title, project, chunks)`, `Commit(hash, repo, subject, author, date)`.\n159\t    Edges (all point at a Project): `IN_PROJECT_S` (Session), `IN_PROJECT_D` (Document),\n160\t    `IN_PROJECT_C` (Commit). Example: `MATCH (c:Commit) RETURN c.subject, c.date ORDER BY c.anchor_seq DESC`.\n161\t    \"\"\"\n162\t    from ..graph import query as _query\n163\t    try:\n164\t        return _query(cypher, limit=limit)\n165\t    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001\n166\t        return {\"error\": str(e), \"hint\": \"the graph may not be built yet\"}\n167\t\n168\t\n169\t@mcp.tool()\n170\tdef threads_open(limit: int = 25) -> dict[str, Any]:\n171\t    \"\"\"List the owner's OPEN loops — current, grounded decisions and commitments that nothing\n172\t    later has superseded — most-stale first, each cited by spine seq. Use this to answer\n173\t    \"what's still open / unresolved for me?\". Only facts the consolidation gate GROUNDED\n174\t    appear here; if empty, either nothing is open or the consolidation pass hasn't run.\n175\t    \"\"\"\n176\t    from ..consolidate import open_threads\n177\t    return {\"threads\": open_threads(SpineStore(), limit=max(1, min(int(limit), 100))),\n178\t            \"provenance\": \"each thread is a grounded consolidation record; cite its `seq` (and `source_seqs`).\"}\n179\t\n180\t\n181\t@mcp.tool()\n182\tdef commitments_due(within_days: int | None = None, limit: int = 50) -> dict[str, Any]:\n183\t    \"\"\"Return the owner's commitment ledger — grounded promises that carry a due date,\n184\t    earliest-due first. `within_days` (optional) limits to those due within that many days\n185\t    from now. Each is cited by spine seq. Answers \"what have I promised, and by when?\".\n186\t    \"\"\"\n187\t    from ..consolidate import due_commitments\n188\t    before = None\n189\t    if within_days is not None:\n190\t        from datetime import datetime, timedelta, timezone\n191\t        before = (datetime.now(timezone.utc) + timedelta(days=int(within_days))).isoformat()\n192\t    return {\"commitments\": due_commitments(SpineStore(), before_iso=before, limit=max(1, min(int(limit), 200))),\n193\t            \"provenance\": \"each commitment is a grounded consolidation record; cite its `seq`.\"}\n194\t\n195\t\n196\t@mcp.tool()\n197\tdef contradictions_pending(limit: int = 25) -> dict[str, Any]:\n198\t    \"\"\"Surface unresolved self-contradictions — subjects on which the owner has more than one\n199\t    live decision. {"parentUuid":"5b26501a-3c51-461e-93e5-1a44dec257e7","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"41d96f36-c558-41bc-8e41-725cff6d0f28","agentId":"a86563067579899f5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01WntMTx7HYZuxi9STB3HXAC","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Append-only, hash-chained JSONL spine (SIGIL §6.1, D1).\n2\t\n3\tReuses CRUCIBLE's tamper-evident chain verbatim (`sigil.reuse`): each line carries\n4\t`{seq, prev_hash, entry_hash}` where `entry_hash` links prev+cert_digest+seq. The\n5\t`cert_digest` is over the record's CONTENT only (scope/kind/source/actor/payload/\n6\tparent/supersedes) — NOT the wallclock `ts` — so the chain is replay-stable. Appends\n7\tare O(1): read the last line's entry, `append_entry`, write.\n8\t\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\timport json\n12\timport os\n13\tfrom pathlib import Path\n14\tfrom typing import Any, Iterator\n15\t\n16\tfrom ..config import SCOPE, SPINE_PATH\n17\tfrom ..reuse import ChainEntry, append_entry, build_chain, digest_payload, verify_chain\n18\tfrom .models import SpineRecord, now_iso\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tdef _last_nonempty_line(path: Path) -> str | None:\n22\t    \"\"\"Read the last non-empty line without loading the file (seek-from-end).\"\"\"\n23\t    with path.open(\"rb\") as f:\n24\t        f.seek(0, os.SEEK_END)\n25\t        end = f.tell()\n26\t        if end == 0:\n27\t            return None\n28\t        buf = b\"\"\n29\t        pos = end\n30\t        while pos > 0:\n31\t            step = min(8192, pos)\n32\t            pos -= step\n33\t            f.seek(pos)\n34\t            buf = f.read(step) + buf\n35\t            lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n36\t            if lines and (pos == 0 or buf.count(b\"\\n\") >= 2):\n37\t                return lines[-1].decode(\"utf-8\")\n38\t        lines = [ln for ln in buf.split(b\"\\n\") if ln.strip()]\n39\t        return lines[-1].decode(\"utf-8\") if lines else None\n40\t\n41\t\n42\tclass SpineStore:\n43\t    def __init__(self, path: Path | str = SPINE_PATH) -> None:\n44\t        self.path = Path(path)\n45\t        self.path.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n46\t        self._last: ChainEntry | None = self._read_last_entry()\n47\t\n48\t    # --- write --------------------------------------------------------------------\n49\t    def append(\n50\t        self, *, kind: str, source: str, actor: str, payload: dict[str, Any],\n51\t        parent_id: int | None = None, supersedes_id: int | None = None,\n52\t        ts: str | None = None,\n53\t    ) -> int:\n54\t        content = {\n55\t            \"scope\": SCOPE, \"kind\": kind, \"source\": source, \"actor\": actor,\n56\t            \"payload\": payload, \"parent_id\": parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": supersedes_id,\n57\t        }\n58\t        cert_digest = digest_payload(content)  # wallclock-free\n59\t        entry = append_entry([self._last], cert_digest) if self._last else build_chain([cert_digest])[0]\n60\t        record = {\n61\t            \"seq\": entry.seq, **content, \"ts\": ts or now_iso(),\n62\t            \"cert_digest\": cert_digest, \"prev_hash\": entry.prev_hash, \"entry_hash\": entry.entry_hash,\n63\t        }\n64\t        with self.path.open(\"a\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n65\t            f.write(json.dumps(record, ensure_ascii=False) + \"\\n\")\n66\t        self._last = entry\n67\t        return entry.seq\n68\t\n69\t    # --- read ---------------------------------------------------------------------\n70\t    def iter_records(self, *, since_seq: int = -1) -> Iterator[SpineRecord]:\n71\t        if not self.path.exists():\n72\t            return\n73\t        with self.path.open(encoding=\"utf-8\") as f:\n74\t            for line in f:\n75\t                line = line.strip()\n76\t                if not line:\n77\t                    continue\n78\t                d = json.loads(line)\n79\t                if d[\"seq\"] > since_seq:\n80\t                    yield SpineRecord.from_dict(d)\n81\t\n82\t    def get(self, seq: int) -> SpineRecord | None:\n83\t        for r in self.iter_records(since_seq=seq - 1):\n84\t            if r.seq == seq:\n85\t                return r\n86\t            if r.seq > seq:\n87\t                break\n88\t        return None\n89\t\n90\t    @property\n91\t    def next_seq(self) -> int:\n92\t        return (self._last.seq + 1) if self._last else 0\n93\t\n94\t    def count(self) -> int:\n95\t        return sum(1 for _ in self.iter_records())\n96\t\n97\t    # --- integrity ----------------------------------------------------------------\n98\t    def entries(self) -> list[ChainEntry]:\n99\t        return [\n100\t            ChainEntry(seq=r.seq, prev_hash=r.prev_hash, cert_digest=r.cert_digest, entry_hash=r.entry_hash)\n101\t            for r in self.iter_records()\n102\t        ]\n103\t\n104\t    def verify(self) -> tuple[bool, str]:\n105\t        \"\"\"Two-layer integrity: (1) BINDING — each record's payload still hashes to its\n106\t        stored cert_digest (catches silent payload edits); (2) CHAIN — the entries link\n107\t        cleanly (catches delete/reorder/entry tamper). A payload edit fails (1); editing\n108\t        the digest to match cascades an entry_hash/prev_hash break caught by (2).\"\"\"\n109\t        entries: list[ChainEntry] = []\n110\t        for r in self.iter_records():\n111\t            content = {\n112\t                \"scope\": r.scope, \"kind\": r.kind, \"source\": r.source, \"actor\": r.actor,\n113\t                \"payload\": r.payload, \"parent_id\": r.parent_id, \"supersedes_id\": r.supersedes_id,\n114\t            }\n115\t            if digest_payload(content) != r.cert_digest:\n116\t                return False, f\"binding break at seq {r.seq}: payload does not match cert_digest (record tampered)\"\n117\t            entries.append(ChainEntry(seq=r.seq, prev_hash=r.prev_hash, cert_digest=r.cert_digest, entry_hash=r.entry_hash))\n118\t        return verify_chain(entries)\n119\t\n120\t    def _read_last_entry(self) -> ChainEntry | None:\n121\t        line = _last_nonempty_line(self.path) if self.path.exists() else None\n122\t        if not line:\n123\t            return None\n124\t        d = json.loads(line)\n125\t        return ChainEntry(seq=d[\"seq\"], prev_hash=d[\"prev_hash\"], cert_digest=d[\"cert_digest\"], entry_hash=d[\"entry_hash\"])\n126\t"}]},"uuid":"943be080-90c5-4f04-bb96-dd2c3a2faedf","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:01:42.992Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"5b26501a-3c51-461e-93e5-1a44dec257e7","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"efc08fd8-9980-44ce-884b-404123e184d0","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"41d96f36-c558-41bc-8e41-725cff6d0f28","agentId":"a86563067579899f5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_019jhCrk3eveueibjzYq61E2","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Read-only queries over the current Kùzu graph (powers the graph.* MCP tools).\n2\t\n3\tOpens `current/` read-only. Every returned entity carries its spine anchor (seq + hash) so\n4\ta graph answer resolves back to tamper-evident memory. `query()` is a guarded Cypher\n5\tpassthrough: writes are refused (both by a keyword guard and by the read-only connection).\n6\t\"\"\"\n7\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n8\t\n9\tfrom typing import Any\n10\t\n11\tfrom .rebuild import CURRENT, _DB\n12\t\n13\t_WRITE_KW = (\"CREATE\", \"SET \", \"DELETE\", \"MERGE\", \"DROP\", \"ALTER\", \"COPY\", \"INSTALL\", \"ATTACH\")\n14\t\n15\t\n16\tclass GraphUnavailable(RuntimeError):\n17\t    \"\"\"The graph has not been rebuilt yet (no current/ db).\"\"\"\n18\t\n19\t\n20\tdef _conn():\n21\t    import kuzu\n22\t    dbfile = CURRENT / _DB\n23\t    if not dbfile.exists():\n24\t        raise GraphUnavailable(\"graph not built yet — run `sigil graph` to rebuild it from the spine\")\n25\t    db = kuzu.Database(str(dbfile), read_only=True)\n26\t    return kuzu.Connection(db)\n27\t\n28\t\n29\tdef _rows(conn, cypher: str, params: dict | None = None) -> list[list[Any]]:\n30\t    res = conn.execute(cypher, parameters=params or {})\n31\t    out = []\n32\t    while res.has_next():\n33\t        out.append(res.get_next())\n34\t    return out\n35\t\n36\t\n37\tdef query(cypher: str, limit: int = 50) -> dict[str, Any]:\n38\t    \"\"\"Run a READ-ONLY Cypher query and return columns + rows. Writes are refused.\"\"\"\n39\t    up = cypher.upper()\n40\t    if any(kw in up for kw in _WRITE_KW):\n41\t        return {\"error\": \"read-only: write/DDL statements are refused\", \"cypher\": cypher}\n42\t    conn = _conn()\n43\t    if \" LIMIT \" not in up:\n44\t        cypher = f\"{cypher.rstrip().rstrip(';')} LIMIT {max(1, min(int(limit), 500))}\"\n45\t    res = conn.execute(cypher, parameters={})\n46\t    cols = res.get_column_names()\n47\t    rows = []\n48\t    while res.has_next():\n49\t        rows.append(res.get_next())\n50\t    return {\"columns\": cols, \"rows\": rows, \"count\": len(rows)}\n51\t\n52\t\n53\tdef _one(conn, cypher, params, keys):\n54\t    r = _rows(conn, cypher, params)\n55\t    return [dict(zip(keys, row)) for row in r]\n56\t\n57\t\n58\tdef entity(name: str) -> dict[str, Any]:\n59\t    \"\"\"Resolve `name` to a structural entity and return it with its neighbours + spine anchor.\n60\t    Tries Project → Session(id) → Commit(hash prefix) → Document(path substring).\"\"\"\n61\t    conn = _conn()\n62\t    # Project\n63\t    proj = _one(conn, \"MATCH (p:Project) WHERE p.name=$n RETURN p.name,p.sessions,p.commits,p.documents,p.messages\",\n64\t                {\"n\": name}, [\"name\", \"sessions\", \"commits\", \"documents\", \"messages\"])\n65\t    if proj:\n66\t        sessions = _one(conn,\n67\t            \"MATCH (s:Session)-[:IN_PROJECT_S]->(p:Project) WHERE p.name=$n \"\n68\t            \"RETURN s.id,s.title,s.messages,s.last_ts,s.anchor_seq ORDER BY s.last_seq DESC LIMIT 25\",\n69\t            {\"n\": name}, [\"id\", \"title\", \"messages\", \"last_ts\", \"anchor_seq\"])\n70\t        commits = _one(conn,\n71\t            \"MATCH (c:Commit)-[:IN_PROJECT_C]->(p:Project) WHERE p.name=$n \"\n72\t            \"RETURN c.hash,c.subject,c.author,c.date,c.anchor_seq ORDER BY c.anchor_seq DESC LIMIT 25\",\n73\t            {\"n\": name}, [\"hash\", \"subject\", \"author\", \"date\", \"anchor_seq\"])\n74\t        docs = _one(conn,\n75\t            \"MATCH (d:Document)-[:IN_PROJECT_D]->(p:Project) WHERE p.name=$n \"\n76\t            \"RETURN d.path,d.title,d.chunks,d.anchor_seq LIMIT 25\",\n77\t            {\"n\": name}, [\"path\", \"title\", \"chunks\", \"anchor_seq\"])\n78\t        return {\"type\": \"Project\", \"entity\": proj[0],\n79\t                \"sessions\": sessions, \"commits\": commits, \"documents\": docs}\n80\t    # Session by id\n81\t    sess = _one(conn,\n82\t        \"MATCH (s:Session) WHERE s.id=$n RETURN s.id,s.title,s.project,s.messages,s.first_ts,s.last_ts,\"\n83\t        \"s.first_seq,s.last_seq,s.anchor_hash\", {\"n\": name},\n84\t        [\"id\", \"title\", \"project\", \"messages\", \"first_ts\", \"last_ts\", \"first_seq\", \"last_seq\", \"anchor_hash\"])\n85\t    if sess:\n86\t        return {\"type\": \"Session\", \"entity\": sess[0],\n87\t                \"hint\": \"read `episodic_range(start_seq=first_seq, end_seq=last_seq)` for the full session\"}\n88\t    # Commit by hash prefix\n89\t    com = _one(conn,\n90\t        \"MATCH (c:Commit) WHERE starts_with(c.hash,$n) RETURN c.hash,c.repo,c.subject,c.author,c.date,c.anchor_seq LIMIT 5\",\n91\t        {\"n\": name}, [\"hash\", \"repo\", \"subject\", \"author\", \"date\", \"anchor_seq\"])\n92\t    if com:\n93\t        return {\"type\": \"Commit\", \"matches\": com}\n94\t    # Document by path substring\n95\t    doc = _one(conn,\n96\t        \"MATCH (d:Document) WHERE contains(d.path,$n) RETURN d.path,d.title,d.project,d.chunks,d.anchor_seq LIMIT 10\",\n97\t        {\"n\": name}, [\"path\", \"title\", \"project\", \"chunks\", \"anchor_seq\"])\n98\t    if doc:\n99\t        return {\"type\": \"Document\", \"matches\": doc}\n100\t    return {\"type\": None, \"note\": f\"no structural entity named/matching '{name}' in the graph\"}\n101\t\n102\t\n103\tdef health() -> dict[str, Any]:\n104\t    \"\"\"Node counts of the current graph + how far it trails the spine head.\"\"\"\n105\t    import json\n106\t\n107\t    from ..spine.store import SpineStore\n108\t    conn = _conn()\n109\t\n110\t    def n(label: str) -> int:\n111\t        r = _rows(conn, f\"MATCH (x:{label}) RETURN count(x)\")\n112\t        return r[0][0] if r else 0\n113\t\n114\t    counts = {lbl: n(lbl) for lbl in (\"Project\", \"Session\", \"Document\", \"Commit\")}\n115\t    manifest = CURRENT / \"manifest.json\"\n116\t    rebuilt_seq = json.loads(manifest.read_text()).get(\"rebuilt_seq\", -1) if manifest.exists() else -1\n117\t    head = SpineStore().next_seq - 1\n118\t    return {\"nodes\": counts, \"rebuilt_through_seq\": rebuilt_seq, \"spine_head_seq\": head,\n119\t            \"in_sync\": rebuilt_seq == head,\n120\t            \"note\": \"the graph is a rebuilt view of the spine; run `sigil graph` to refresh it\"}\n121\t"}]},"uuid":"57b833a7-9542-4891-991f-36ddc34c56ce","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:01:43.434Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"efc08fd8-9980-44ce-884b-404123e184d0","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

An agent\n2\tQUEUES a proposal (governor → QUEUE); the owner APPROVES or DENIES it here. Authentication is an\n3\tEd25519 signature over the canonical (target, decision, approver) by the OWNER key.\n4\t\n5\tRED-PEN HARDENING (Phase 6):\n6\t • The trusted pubkey is the PERSISTED owner identity — NOT the key supplied to the queue, so an\n7\t   attacker cannot self-certify by bringing their own key (RP-APPROVAL-2). approve/deny require the\n8\t   supplied signing key to BE the trusted owner key.\n9\t • `pending()` treats a queued item as resolved ONLY when a superseding approval VERIFIES against the\n10\t   trusted owner key, and keys resolution off the SIGNED target_seq (not the raw supersedes_id) — so\n11\t   an unsigned/forged approval can't silently drop an item (RP-1/RP-APPROVAL-1), and a genuine\n12\t   approval of one item can't be replayed onto another (RP-APPROVAL-4). `verify_approval` is thereby\n13\t   on the enforcement path (RP-APPROVAL-3).\n14\t\n15\tThis records the DECISION; it executes no external effect (SIGIL has no send/deploy path). The\n16\ttransport (Telegram/WhatsApp over WireGuard, §9.3) is a seam over this authenticated core.\"\"\"\n17\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n18\t\n19\tfrom typing import List, Optional\n20\t\n21\tfrom ..reuse import canonical_json, sha256_hex, sign, verify_one\n22\tfrom ..spine.store import SpineStore\n23\t\n24\tSIGNAL = \"governor.approval\"\n25\t_QUEUED_STATUS = \"awaiting-approval\"\n26\t\n27\t\n28\tdef _approval_message(target_seq, decision: str, approver: str) -> bytes:\n29\t    m = canonical_json({\"target\": target_seq, \"decision\": decision, \"approver\": approver})\n30\t    return m if isinstance(m, bytes) else m.encode()\n31\t\n32\t\n33\tdef verify_approval(record, trusted_pubkey_b64: Optional[str]) -> bool:\n34\t    \"\"\"True iff the approval carries a valid OWNER signature over its (target, decision, approver).\n35\t    Unsigned, wrong-key, or no-trusted-key → False (fail-closed).\"\"\"\n36\t    p = record.payload if hasattr(record, \"payload\") else record\n37\t    sig = p.get(\"sig\")\n38\t    if not sig or not trusted_pubkey_b64 or p.get(\"pubkey\") != trusted_pubkey_b64:\n39\t        return False\n40\t    msg = _approval_message(p.get(\"target_seq\"), p.get(\"approval\"), p.get(\"approver\"))\n41\t    return verify_one(trusted_pubkey_b64, msg, sig)\n42\t\n43\t\n44\tdef pending(store: SpineStore, trusted_pubkey_b64: Optional[str] = None) -> List:\n45\t    \"\"\"Queued proposals with NO valid owner approval yet, oldest first. Resolution requires a\n46\t    VERIFIED approval; an unsigned/forged/wrong-key approval leaves the item pending (fail-closed).\"\"\"\n47\t    if trusted_pubkey_b64 is None:\n48\t        from ..governor.identity import owner_pubkey\n49\t        trusted_pubkey_b64 = owner_pubkey()\n50\t    resolved = set()\n51\t    queued = {}\n52\t    for r in store.iter_records():\n53\t        p = r.payload\n54\t        if p.get(\"signal\") == SIGNAL and verify_approval(r, trusted_pubkey_b64):\n55\t            resolved.add(p.get(\"target_seq\"))       # honor the SIGNED target, not raw supersedes_id\n56\t        if p.get(\"decision\") == \"queued\" and p.get(\"status\") == _QUEUED_STATUS:\n57\t            queued[r.seq] = r\n58\t    return [r for seq, r in sorted(queued.items()) if seq not in resolved]\n59\t\n60\t\n61\tclass ApprovalError(Exception):\n62\t    pass\n63\t\n64\t\n65\tclass ApprovalQueue:\n66\t    def __init__(self, store: Optional[SpineStore] = None, *, owner_key=None,\n67\t                 trusted_pubkey_b64: Optional[str] = None):\n68\t        from ..governor.identity import owner_keypair, owner_pubkey\n69\t        self.store = store or SpineStore()\n70\t        self.owner_key = owner_key if owner_key is not None else owner_keypair()\n71\t        # PINNED to the persisted owner identity — never defaulted to the supplied key (RP-APPROVAL-2)\n72\t        self.trusted_pubkey_b64 = trusted_pubkey_b64 if trusted_pubkey_b64 is not None else owner_pubkey()\n73\t\n74\t    def _target(self, seq: int):\n75\t        for r in pending(self.store, self.trusted_pubkey_b64):\n76\t            if r.seq == seq:\n77\t                return r\n78\t        raise ApprovalError(f\"seq {seq} is not a pending approval (already decided, or not queued)\")\n79\t\n80\t    def _decide(self, seq: int, decision: str, *, approver: str, reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n81\t        target = self._target(seq)\n82\t        # the signing key MUST be the trusted owner key — not merely \"some key present\" (RP-APPROVAL-2).\n83\t        if (self.owner_key is None or self.trusted_pubkey_b64 is None\n84\t                or self.owner_key.public_key_b64 != self.trusted_pubkey_b64):\n85\t            raise ApprovalError(\"approval requires the OWNER's signing key (missing or not the trusted key)\")\n86\t        msg = _approval_message(seq, decision, approver)\n87\t        sig = sign(self.owner_key.private_key_b64, msg)\n88\t        payload = {\"signal\": SIGNAL, \"approval\": decision, \"target_seq\": seq, \"target_kind\": target.kind,\n89\t                   \"target_tier\": target.payload.get(\"tier\"), \"approver\": approver, \"reason\": reason,\n90\t                   \"pubkey\": self.trusted_pubkey_b64, \"sig\": sig, \"msg_digest\": sha256_hex(msg),\n91\t                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}\n92\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"OWNER\",\n93\t                                 payload=payload, supersedes_id=seq)\n94\t\n95\t    def approve(self, seq: int, *, approver: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n96\t        return self._decide(seq, \"approved\", approver=approver, reason=reason)\n97\t\n98\t    def deny(self, seq: int, *, approver: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n99\t        return self._decide(seq, \"denied\", approver=approver, reason=reason)\n100\t"}]},"uuid":"2303344a-4bfc-4931-9970-1b07d138a0e8","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:01:52.638Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"c6d26765-cfdb-42f8-9bc9-904b57970d7d","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"24fb86ee-55ad-415c-a20d-43bbc404ffd5","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"41d96f36-c558-41bc-8e41-725cff6d0f28","agentId":"a86563067579899f5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01XUehWwhaunPtziMAV1xBwS","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Owner identity for governance authentication (Phase 6). The trust anchor is the SAME solo-owner\n2\tEd25519 keypair the spine checkpoint already persists (`KEYS_DIR/owner.priv|pub`, the 1-of-1 trust\n3\troot) — governance events (promotion grants, kill release, approvals) are signed by it and verified\n4\tagainst it. Reads are fail-closed: a missing key returns None, so nothing forged is ever trusted.\n5\t\n6\t`owner_pubkey()`/`owner_keypair()` READ the anchor (never generate — verification must not mint\n7\ttrust). `ensure_owner_keypair()` is for owner-initiated SIGNING actions (CLI engage/grant/approve):\n8\tit generates+persists the anchor once if absent, mirroring the checkpoint's `_owner_keys()`.\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\timport os\n12\tfrom typing import Optional\n13\t\n14\tfrom ..config import KEYS_DIR\n15\tfrom ..reuse import KeyPair, generate_keypair\n16\t\n17\t_PRIV = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.priv\"\n18\t_PUB = KEYS_DIR / \"owner.pub\"\n19\t\n20\t\n21\tdef owner_pubkey() -> Optional[str]:\n22\t    try:\n23\t        return (_PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip() or None)\n24\t    except OSError:\n25\t        return None\n26\t\n27\t\n28\tdef owner_keypair() -> Optional[KeyPair]:\n29\t    try:\n30\t        priv = _PRIV.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n31\t        pub = _PUB.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\").strip()\n32\t    except OSError:\n33\t        return None\n34\t    return KeyPair(public_key_b64=pub, private_key_b64=priv) if priv and pub else None\n35\t\n36\t\n37\tdef ensure_owner_keypair() -> KeyPair:\n38\t    \"\"\"Return the persisted owner keypair, generating+persisting it once if absent (owner signing\n39\t    path only). Same key material the checkpoint uses, so governance and the spine head share one\n40\t    owner identity.\"\"\"\n41\t    kp = owner_keypair()\n42\t    if kp is not None:\n43\t        return kp\n44\t    KEYS_DIR.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n45\t    kp = generate_keypair()\n46\t    _PRIV.write_text(kp.private_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n47\t    _PUB.write_text(kp.public_key_b64, encoding=\"utf-8\")\n48\t    for f in (_PRIV,):\n49\t        try:\n50\t            os.chmod(f, 0o600)\n51\t        except OSError:\n52\t            pass\n53\t    return kp\n54\t"}]},"uuid":"1b4a036e-976b-4f19-aaf1-f9d241a271ec","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:01:59.685Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"24fb86ee-55ad-415c-a20d-43bbc404ffd5","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"1ca90b90-5b72-4e74-a621-a95b6cd3d540","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"41d96f36-c558-41bc-8e41-725cff6d0f28","agentId":"a86563067579899f5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01BjoqBHaEx2t1n33h3VGzGi","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"The kill switch (SIGIL §5) — a single latch that halts the agent mesh while leaving perception and\n2\tmemory-read (A0 observe) alive. State is append-only on the spine.\n3\t\n4\tASYMMETRIC AUTHENTICATION (Phase 6 red-pen RP-2): halting is always the safe direction, so ANY\n5\tengage event halts (a nuisance forged-engage is at worst a fail-safe DoS). UN-halting is the\n6\tdangerous direction, so a RELEASE is honored ONLY if it is signed by the owner key and verifies\n7\tagainst the trusted pubkey — a forged release can never revive a halted mesh. Read fresh per decision\n8\tso a release (or engage) takes effect immediately.\"\"\"\n9\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n10\t\n11\tfrom typing import Optional\n12\t\n13\tfrom .authn import signed_payload, verify_signed\n14\tfrom .identity import owner_keypair, owner_pubkey\n15\t\n16\tSIGNAL = \"governor.killswitch\"\n17\t_CORE = (\"signal\", \"state\")\n18\t\n19\t\n20\tclass KillSwitch:\n21\t    def __init__(self, store, *, owner_key=None, trusted_pubkey: Optional[str] = None):\n22\t        self.store = store\n23\t        self.owner_key = owner_key if owner_key is not None else owner_keypair()\n24\t        self.trusted_pubkey = trusted_pubkey if trusted_pubkey is not None else owner_pubkey()\n25\t\n26\t    def engage(self, *, by: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n27\t        core = {\"signal\": SIGNAL, \"state\": \"engaged\"}\n28\t        payload = {**signed_payload(core, self.owner_key), \"by\": by, \"reason\": reason,\n29\t                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}\n30\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\", payload=payload)\n31\t\n32\t    def release(self, *, by: str = \"owner\", reason: str = \"\") -> int:\n33\t        core = {\"signal\": SIGNAL, \"state\": \"released\"}\n34\t        payload = {**signed_payload(core, self.owner_key), \"by\": by, \"reason\": reason,\n35\t                   \"tier\": \"A0\", \"decision\": \"auto\"}\n36\t        return self.store.append(kind=\"event\", source=\"governor\", actor=\"WARDEN\", payload=payload)\n37\t\n38\t    def is_engaged(self) -> bool:\n39\t        engaged = False\n40\t        for r in self.store.iter_records():\n41\t            p = r.payload\n42\t            if p.get(\"signal\") != SIGNAL:\n43\t                continue\n44\t            state = p.get(\"state\")\n45\t            if state == \"engaged\":\n46\t                engaged = True                      # honor ANY engage — halting is fail-safe\n47\t            elif state == \"released\" and verify_signed(p, _CORE, self.trusted_pubkey):\n48\t                engaged = False                     # only an OWNER-SIGNED release un-halts (fail-closed)\n49\t        return engaged\n50\t"}]},"uuid":"29500f24-659b-4e59-94e5-d1443bf89498","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:02:00.110Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"1ca90b90-5b72-4e74-a621-a95b6cd3d540","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

{"parentUuid":"30beefab-8de6-4571-9211-ff68139c7c73","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"41d96f36-c558-41bc-8e41-725cff6d0f28","agentId":"a86563067579899f5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01DEK9jQ9rZkmCy3eRWPBBy4","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t\"\"\"Capture backends (SIGIL §8). A `Frame` is the immutable record of one capture: the image bytes'\n2\tsha256 (integrity), the OCR/accessibility TEXT (the GROUND TRUTH a query is answered from), and a\n3\tpath to the image. Real backends shell out to whatever is installed (screenshot tool + tesseract,\n4\tv4l2/ffmpeg); every backend returns `None` on any failure — a missing camera is no capture, never a\n5\tfabricated one (same posture as SCHOLAR.read_source). `StaticFrame` is the deterministic test double.\n6\t\n7\tHONEST GAPS: headless hosts often lack a screenshot tool / tesseract / a camera, so the real\n8\tbackends degrade to `None` or an image-only Frame (text=\"\"). The richest real screen source is the\n9\tOS accessibility tree (C4); it is not available on a headless box and is left as a documented seam.\"\"\"\n10\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n11\t\n12\timport shutil\n13\timport subprocess\n14\timport tempfile\n15\tfrom dataclasses import dataclass\n16\tfrom pathlib import Path\n17\tfrom typing import Optional\n18\t\n19\tfrom ..reuse import sha256_hex\n20\t\n21\t_SCREENSHOT_TOOLS = (\n22\t    (\"scrot\", [\"scrot\", \"-o\"]),\n23\t    (\"gnome-screenshot\", [\"gnome-screenshot\", \"-f\"]),\n24\t    (\"spectacle\", [\"spectacle\", \"-b\", \"-n\", \"-o\"]),\n25\t    (\"import\", [\"import\", \"-window\", \"root\"]),   # ImageMagick\n26\t)\n27\t\n28\t\n29\t@dataclass(frozen=True)\n30\tclass Frame:\n31\t    kind: str                       # \"screen\" | \"camera\"\n32\t    sha256: str                     # integrity of the captured image bytes\n33\t    text: str                       # OCR / accessibility text — the GROUND TRUTH; \"\" if none\n34\t    image_path: Optional[str] = None\n35\t    width: int = 0\n36\t    height: int = 0\n37\t\n38\t    @classmethod\n39\t    def from_image(cls, kind: str, image_path: str, *, text: str = \"\") -> \"Frame\":\n40\t        data = Path(image_path).read_bytes()\n41\t        return cls(kind=kind, sha256=sha256_hex(data), text=text, image_path=image_path)\n42\t\n43\t\n44\tdef _ocr(image_path: str) -> str:\n45\t    \"\"\"Extract text via tesseract if present; '' otherwise (no OCR is not a failure of capture).\"\"\"\n46\t    if not shutil.which(\"tesseract\"):\n47\t        return \"\"\n48\t    try:\n49\t        proc = subprocess.run([\"tesseract\", image_path, \"stdout\"],\n50\t                              capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=30)\n51\t        return (proc.stdout or \"\").strip()\n52\t    except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError):\n53\t        return \"\"\n54\t\n55\t\n56\tdef grab_screen() -> Optional[Frame]:\n57\t    \"\"\"Screenshot the current display + OCR it. Returns None if no screenshot tool is available\n58\t    or the grab fails. The accessibility-tree path (richer, C4) is a documented seam, not wired\n59\t    on headless hosts.\"\"\"\n60\t    out = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".png\", prefix=\"sigil-screen-\")\n61\t    for name, argv in _SCREENSHOT_TOOLS:\n62\t        if not shutil.which(name):\n63\t            continue\n64\t        try:\n65\t            proc = subprocess.run([*argv, out], capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)\n66\t        except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError):\n67\t            continue\n68\t        if proc.returncode == 0 and Path(out).exists() and Path(out).stat().st_size > 0:\n69\t            return Frame.from_image(\"screen\", out, text=_ocr(out))\n70\t    return None\n71\t\n72\t\n73\tdef grab_camera(device: str = \"/dev/video0\") -> Optional[Frame]:\n74\t    \"\"\"Grab a single frame from a v4l2 camera via ffmpeg. Returns None if ffmpeg or the device is\n75\t    absent, or the grab fails. Camera frames rarely carry text, so OCR is best-effort.\"\"\"\n76\t    if not shutil.which(\"ffmpeg\") or not Path(device).exists():\n77\t        return None\n78\t    out = tempfile.mktemp(suffix=\".png\", prefix=\"sigil-cam-\")\n79\t    try:\n80\t        proc = subprocess.run(\n81\t            [\"ffmpeg\", \"-y\", \"-f\", \"v4l2\", \"-i\", device, \"-frames:v\", \"1\", out],\n82\t            capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=20)\n83\t    except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError):\n84\t        return None\n85\t    if proc.returncode == 0 and Path(out).exists() and Path(out).stat().st_size > 0:\n86\t        return Frame.from_image(\"camera\", out, text=_ocr(out))\n87\t    return None\n88\t\n89\t\n90\tdef StaticFrame(*, kind: str = \"screen\", text: str = \"\", tag: str = \"\") -> Frame:\n91\t    \"\"\"Deterministic test/double frame — no filesystem, sha256 derived from (tag or text) so\n92\t    identical content hashes identically (drives ambient change-detection).\"\"\"\n93\t    return Frame(kind=kind, sha256=sha256_hex((tag or text).encode()), text=text, image_path=None)\n94\t"}]},"uuid":"22dd020c-ade2-4c8c-880f-f85ad0a1173d","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:02:00.213Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"30beefab-8de6-4571-9211-ff68139c7c73","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}

Recognized text is routed through the Phase-1 KERNEL (`sigil-kernel\n2\task`), so a voice request crosses the SAME T0 router + WARDEN gate + signed action log as any\n3\tother — voice is just another interface onto the one authorized path. The spoken response is the\n4\tKERNEL's answer body (the bracketed [T0…]/[WARDEN…] status lines are stripped).\"\"\"\n5\tfrom __future__ import annotations\n6\t\n7\timport subprocess\n8\tfrom pathlib import Path\n9\t\n10\t\n11\tdef _default_bin() -> str:\n12\t    for p in (\"kernel/target/release/sigil-kernel\", \"kernel/target/debug/sigil-kernel\"):\n13\t        f = Path(\"/home/kali/sigil\") / p\n14\t        if f.exists():\n15\t            return str(f)\n16\t    return \"sigil-kernel\"\n17\t\n18\t\n19\tclass KernelDispatch:\n20\t    def __init__(self, kernel_bin: str | None = None, timeout: int = 60):\n21\t        self.kernel_bin = kernel_bin or _default_bin()\n22\t        self.timeout = timeout\n23\t\n24\t    # exact KERNEL status-line prefixes to strip (so a legitimate answer line that merely starts\n25\t    # with '[' is NOT dropped, and a BLOCKED/error is NOT masked as an answer).\n26\t    _STATUS = (\"[t0\", \"[warden\", \"[blocked\", \"[direct\", \"[dispatch\")\n27\t\n28\t    def send(self, text: str) -> str:\n29\t        text = (text or \"\").strip()\n30\t        if not text:\n31\t            return \"I didn't catch that.\"\n32\t        try:\n33\t            proc = subprocess.run([self.kernel_bin, \"ask\", text],\n34\t                                  capture_output=True, text=True, timeout=self.timeout)\n35\t        except (subprocess.SubprocessError, OSError) as e:\n36\t            return f\"the kernel is unavailable ({e})\"\n37\t        if proc.returncode != 0:\n38\t            tail = (proc.stderr or proc.stdout).strip().splitlines()\n39\t            return f\"that request was refused or errored: {tail[-1][:200]}\" if tail else \"that request was refused.\"\n40\t        if any(ln.lstrip().lower().startswith(\"[blocked\") for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines()):\n41\t            return \"that action needs your approval — it wasn't run.\"\n42\t        body = [ln.strip() for ln in proc.stdout.splitlines()\n43\t                if ln.strip() and not any(ln.lstrip().lower().startswith(s) for s in self._STATUS)]\n44\t        answer = \" \".join(body).strip()\n45\t        return answer[:600] if answer else \"there's no answer for that in memory yet.\"\n46\t"}]},"uuid":"75251ecb-fc73-4928-890c-fe5be4976d9e","timestamp":"2026-07-18T17:02:09.863Z","sourceToolAssistantUUID":"2850f4f7-5c54-4e86-a36f-0ff09aaf9e11","userType":"external","entrypoint":"claude-vscode","cwd":"/home/kali/Pictures/PENTEST-main","sessionId":"7758e121-f349-47d5-886b-6bb5a1d60e27","version":"2.1.214","gitBranch":"main","slug":"parsed-popping-lemur"}
{"parentUuid":"1db81c5a-341a-4c94-82f2-694c600fe6ee","isSidechain":true,"promptId":"41d96f36-c558-41bc-8e41-725cff6d0f28","agentId":"a86563067579899f5","type":"user","message":{"role":"user","content":[{"tool_use_id":"toolu_01N912fJ5J6ob8YVyCUxJK7H","type":"tool_result","content":"1\t//! WARDEN autonomy tiers (SIGIL §5). Every tool invocation is classified A0–A3; the gate\n2\t//! decision follows from the tier. FAIL-CLOSED and TOKEN-BASED: the tool name is split into\n3\t//! whole tokens (on `.`/`_`/`-`/`/`/space) and matched against whole-token sets — never a raw\n4\t//! substring, so \"overwrite\" is not \"write\" and \"forget\" is not \"get\". Danger is checked FIRST,\n5\t//! and A0 (auto, un-queued) is reachable ONLY via a positive safe-verb allowlist; anything not\n6\t//! positively classified — including any unknown or dangerous-target tool — is A3.\n7\t\n8\tuse std::fmt;\n9\t\n10\tuse serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};\n11\t\n12\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n13\tpub enum Tier {\n14\t    /// Observe / answer — memory queries, screen read, voice reply. Auto.\n15\t    A0,\n16\t    /// Reversible internal act — write a report/brief, draft-branch, raise an alert. Auto + logged.\n17\t    A1,\n18\t    /// External-visible / semi-reversible — send email, calendar write, purchase < cap. Queued.\n19\t    A2,\n20\t    /// Destructive / financial / security — push protected branch, deploy, delete, spend > cap. Explicit.\n21\t    A3,\n22\t}\n23\t\n24\timpl Tier {\n25\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n26\t        match self {\n27\t            Tier::A0 => \"A0\",\n28\t            Tier::A1 => \"A1\",\n29\t            Tier::A2 => \"A2\",\n30\t            Tier::A3 => \"A3\",\n31\t        }\n32\t    }\n33\t}\n34\t\n35\timpl fmt::Display for Tier {\n36\t    fn fmt(&self, f: &mut fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> fmt::Result {\n37\t        f.write_str(self.as_str())\n38\t    }\n39\t}\n40\t\n41\t#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]\n42\tpub enum Decision {\n43\t    Auto,\n44\t    Queued,\n45\t    ExplicitRequired,\n46\t}\n47\t\n48\timpl Decision {\n49\t    pub fn as_str(&self) -> &'static str {\n50\t        match self {\n51\t            Decision::Auto => \"auto\",\n52\t            Decision::Queued => \"queued\",\n53\t            Decision::ExplicitRequired => \"explicit-required\",\n54\t        }\n55\t    }\n56\t    pub fn may_run(&self) -> bool {\n57\t        matches!(self, Decision::Auto)\n58\t    }\n59\t}\n60\t\n61\t/// A3 — destructive verbs, financial ops, crypto/restore ops, and DANGEROUS TARGETS\n62\t/// (secret/identity/network/prod material is A3 regardless of the verb: `secrets.read`,\n63\t/// `iam.policy.write`, `budget.get`, `vault.read`).\n64\tconst A3_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n65\t    // destructive verbs\n66\t    \"push\", \"deploy\", \"delete\", \"destroy\", \"drop\", \"remove\", \"purge\", \"wipe\", \"truncate\",\n67\t    \"overwrite\", \"erase\", \"format\", \"kill\", \"shutdown\", \"reboot\", \"reset\", \"disable\", \"enable\",\n68\t    \"override\", \"force\", \"sudo\", \"exec\", \"eval\", \"chmod\", \"chown\", \"patch\", \"install\", \"uninstall\",\n69\t    // crypto + restore/rollback (a restore silently reverts current state)\n70\t    \"encrypt\", \"decrypt\", \"restore\", \"revert\", \"rollback\", \"recover\",\n71\t    // financial\n72\t    \"spend\", \"purchase\", \"pay\", \"payment\", \"transaction\", \"transfer\", \"refund\", \"invoice\",\n73\t    \"allocate\", \"budget\", \"release\", \"sign\",\n74\t    // security / identity / infra / secret-store TARGETS (dangerous no matter the verb)\n75\t    \"secret\", \"secrets\", \"credential\", \"credentials\", \"token\", \"tokens\", \"key\", \"keys\", \"iam\",\n76\t    \"policy\", \"firewall\", \"acl\", \"role\", \"grant\", \"revoke\", \"rotate\", \"escalate\", \"infra\",\n77\t    \"prod\", \"production\", \"env\", \"master\", \"root\", \"admin\",\n78\t    \"vault\", \"keyring\", \"keychain\", \"keystore\", \"hsm\",\n79\t];\n80\t\n81\t/// A2 — external-visible / semi-reversible: communication, publishing, and bulk DATA EGRESS\n82\t/// (export/dump of a private store must be human-seen, never auto).\n83\tconst A2_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n84\t    \"send\", \"email\", \"smtp\", \"publish\", \"post\", \"message\", \"outbound\", \"webhook\", \"sms\", \"notify\",\n85\t    \"share\", \"upload\", \"invite\", \"calendar\", \"tweet\", \"dm\", \"export\", \"dump\", \"download\", \"sync\",\n86\t];\n87\t\n88\t/// A1 — reversible internal writes (drafts, notes, memory writes, non-push commits). NOTE:\n89\t/// \"snapshot\" is intentionally NOT here — a snapshot RESTORE is destructive (caught by A3\n90\t/// \"restore\"), and snapshot-create alone falls to fail-closed A3 rather than risk auto-run.\n91\tconst A1_TOKENS: &[&str] = &[\n92\t    \"write\", \"note\", \"brief\", \"report\", \"draft\", \"alert\", \"consolidate\", \"commit\", \"branch\",\n93\t    \"annotate\", \"tag\", \"label\",\n94\t];\n95\t\n96\t/// A0 — POSITIVE allowlist of known-safe observe/answer VERBS only (NO target nouns — a target\n97\t/// noun here would let e.g. `memory.encrypt` auto-run). A tool reaches A0 only by a read-verb\n98\t/// here, or an exact name in `A0_TOOLS`; absence of danger alone is NOT sufficient → fail-closed A3.\n99\tconst A0_VERBS: &[&str] = &[\n100\t    \"read\", \"search\", \"query\", \"get\", \"list\", \"status\", \"recall\", \"observe\", \"answer\",\n101\t    \"view\", \"show\", \"find\", \"frame\", \"peek\", \"describe\", \"inspect\", \"lookup\",\n102\t];\n103\t\n104\t/// A0 — exact-name allowlist for the known read-only memory tools whose names are not verb-clean\n105\t/// (`graph.entity`, `episodic.range`, `threads.open`, `commitments.due`, `contradictions.pending`,\n106\t/// `ingest.status`). Matched on the whole lowercased tool name.\n107\tconst A0_TOOLS: &[&str] = &[\n108\t    \"memory.search\", \"graph.query\", \"graph.entity\", \"episodic.range\", \"ingest.status\",\n109\t    \"threads.open\", \"commitments.due\", \"contradictions.pending\",\n110\t];\n111\t\n112\t/// Split a tool name into whole tokens on `.`/`_`/`-`/`/` and whitespace, lowercased.\n113\tfn tokens(tool: &str) -> Vec<String> {\n114\t    tool.split(|c: char| c == '.' || c == '_' || c == '-' || c == '/' || c.is_whitespace())\n115\t        .filter(|s| !s.is_empty())\n116\t        .map(|s| s.to_ascii_lowercase())\n117\t        .collect()\n118\t}\n119\t\n120\t/// Classify a tool name into a tier. Danger FIRST, then A2, A1; A0 only via a positive safe-verb\n121\t/// or an exact safe-tool name; everything else (unknown / not-positively-safe / empty) → A3.\n122\tpub fn classify(tool: &str) -> Tier {\n123\t    let full = tool.to_ascii_lowercase();\n124\t    let tk = tokens(tool);\n125\t    if tk.is_empty() {\n126\t        return Tier::A3;\n127\t    }\n128\t    let has = |set: &[&str]| tk.iter().any(|t| set.contains(&t.as_str()));\n129\t    if has(A3_TOKENS) {\n130\t        return Tier::A3;\n131\t    }\n132\t    if has(A2_TOKENS) {\n133\t        return Tier::A2;\n134\t    }\n135\t    if has(A1_TOKENS) {\n136\t        return Tier::A1;\n137\t    }\n138\t    if A0_TOOLS.contains(&full.as_str()) || has(A0_VERBS) {\n139\t        return Tier::A0;\n140\t    }\n141\t    Tier::A3 // not positively classified → fail-closed to the most-gated tier\n142\t}\n143\t\n144\tpub fn gate(tier: Tier) -> Decision {\n145\t    match tier {\n146\t        Tier::A0 | Tier::A1 => Decision::Auto,\n147\t        Tier::A2 => Decision::Queued,\n148\t        Tier::A3 => Decision::ExplicitRequired,\n149\t    }\n150\t}\n151\t\n152\t#[cfg(test)]\n153\tmod tests {\n154\t    use super::*;\n155\t\n156\t    #[test]\n157\t    fn classification_matches_spec_examples() {\n158\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.search\"), Tier::A0);\n159\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"graph.query\"), Tier::A0);\n160\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.write\"), Tier::A1);\n161\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"brief.compose\"), Tier::A1);\n162\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"email.send\"), Tier::A2);\n163\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"calendar.write\"), Tier::A2); // \"calendar\" (A2) beats \"write\" (A1)\n164\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"git.push\"), Tier::A3);\n165\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"deploy.prod\"), Tier::A3);\n166\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"data.delete\"), Tier::A3);\n167\t    }\n168\t\n169\t    #[test]\n170\t    fn unknown_and_empty_are_fail_closed_a3() {\n171\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"something.unclassified\"), Tier::A3);\n172\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"\"), Tier::A3);\n173\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"weird\"), Tier::A3);\n174\t        assert_eq!(gate(classify(\"something.unclassified\")), Decision::ExplicitRequired);\n175\t    }\n176\t\n177\t    #[test]\n178\t    fn substring_collisions_do_not_lower_the_tier() {\n179\t        // the exact review findings: a dangerous op must NOT ride a benign substring down a tier\n180\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"config.overwrite\"), Tier::A3, \"overwrite != write\");\n181\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"db.overwrite\"), Tier::A3);\n182\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"files.forget\"), Tier::A3, \"forget != get; fail-closed\");\n183\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"budget.override\"), Tier::A3, \"financial + override\");\n184\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"budget.get\"), Tier::A3, \"financial target is A3 regardless of verb\");\n185\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"iam.policy.write\"), Tier::A3, \"identity write is A3, not A1\");\n186\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"firewall.rule.write\"), Tier::A3);\n187\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"transaction.sign\"), Tier::A3, \"financial signing is A3, not A1\");\n188\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"secrets.read\"), Tier::A3, \"secret read is A3, not A0\");\n189\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"credentials.get\"), Tier::A3);\n190\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"account.disable\"), Tier::A3);\n191\t    }\n192\t\n193\t    #[test]\n194\t    fn dangerous_ops_on_safe_targets_do_not_auto_run() {\n195\t        // the CRITICAL re-check finding: a target noun must NOT grant A0 to a dangerous verb\n196\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.encrypt\"), Tier::A3, \"ransomware-shaped op must NOT be A0\");\n197\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"graph.destroy\"), Tier::A3);\n198\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"entity.merge\"), Tier::A3, \"irreversible rewrite → fail-closed, not A0\");\n199\t        assert_eq!(classify(\"memory.export\"), Tier::A2, \"full-store egress must be queued,
