{"parentUuid":"a6b731d4-7012-45a6-841b-2679dc00fb50","isSidechain":true,"agentId":"a86563067579899f5","message":{"model":"claude-opus-4-8","id":"msg_011Cd9tBNSX9fVgGvg4q9mdn","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I have verified all the load-bearing signatures and posture. I have everything needed to design both workstreams grounded in the real substrate. Here is the design document.\n\n---\n\n# SIGIL Workstreams 3 & 4 — Peak-Innovative Build Plan\n\nThe whole design rests on one observation from the substrate: **SIGIL already contains every hard part in a headless form.** `dashboard.snapshot()` is the entire cockpit JSON contract; `mcp/server.py` is a fully-worked read-only/fail-closed/provenance-carrying network surface (the exact posture to mirror); `ApprovalQueue`/`KillSwitch` are owner-signed and RP-hardened; `graph.query` is a guarded read-only Cypher passthrough; `KernelDispatch.send` is a proven text→authorized-KERNEL seam; `tiers.rs` already classifies notify/webhook/message as A2. Both workstreams are therefore **new surfaces onto existing authorized cores, plus two genuinely new primitives** (a spine-tail, and a signed device/host ledger). Nothing here invents a new authority path — that is the doctrine constraint made into the design principle.\n\n---\n\n## 0. Shared foundation — design once, power both workstreams\n\nThree primitives are built first and consumed by both the UI and the mobile bridge. This is the \"peak-innovative but not duplicated\" core.\n\n### 0.1 The spine-tail primitive (`SpineTailer`) — a real tail over an append-only poll-only log\nThe spine is poll-only: `iter_records(since_seq=N)` yields `seq>N`, `next_seq` is the head cursor. There is no SSE/inotify/tail today. The primitive turns the cursor into an **event source** that is itself provenance-proving:\n\n- Holds a cursor (`last_emitted_seq`) and the last emitted `entry_hash`.\n- On each coalesced tick (~250 ms — \"cheap-local\"), calls `iter_records(since_seq=cursor)`; for each new record it **verifies chain-linkage** (`record.prev_hash == last_emitted.entry_hash`, and re-derives `cert_digest` to confirm `entry_hash`) *before* emitting. A tampered, rewound, or forked spine is caught at the transport layer — \"prove-don't-guess\" enforced on the live edge, not just at rest.\n- Emits records already shaped like the MCP tool output (`seq, kind, source, actor, ts, entry_hash, text()`), so consumers get cited atoms.\n- Fan-out to N subscribers with per-subscriber bounded queues (drop-oldest + resync-from-cursor on overflow, never fabricate a gap).\n\nThis ONE primitive powers the UI live feed (SSE) **and** the mobile push notifier. It is pure (no server), so it is the safest possible first slice to build and red-pen.\n\n### 0.2 The owner-signed action broker — the single gated-action funnel\nEvery gated action from any new surface (browser button, phone tap) routes through one module that mirrors `cli.py::cmd_approve`/`cmd_warden` exactly. It is where owner-key handling, CSRF/Origin/token proof, and tier prediction live **once**. The UI action plane and the mobile daemon are both thin callers of this broker. The private key never leaves the process that the owner started; the surface only carries an authenticated *request* to sign.\n\n### 0.3 A shared \"re-verify this atom\" helper\nA tiny function `verify_record(record) -> (ok, reason)` that re-derives `cert_digest`/`entry_hash` for a single record (reusing `reuse.digest_payload` + the chain check already inside `SpineStore.verify`). Used by the UI `/api/record` endpoint, the tailer, and the mobile daemon so \"serve-the-quote\" is one implementation, not three.\n\nEvery new module calls `assert_no_offense()` at import (doctrine §12), same as `mcp/server.py:21`.\n\n---\n\n## WORKSTREAM 3 — REAL UI (loopback glass cockpit)\n\n### 3.1 Peak-innovative core mechanisms\n\n1. **Provenance-first rendering (serve-the-quote made literal).** Every displayed atom carries `data-seq`/`data-hash` and click-throughs to `GET /api/record/{seq}`, which returns the raw `SpineRecord` and re-verifies its `entry_hash` on the fly (0.3). If re-verify fails, the atom is badged \"integrity broken\" rather than shown as truth. There is no fact on screen that does not resolve to a real spine `entry_hash`. This is the UI expression of doctrine §1.5.\n\n2. **A live event stream built as a real tail primitive (0.1) exposed over SSE.** SSE (`text/event-stream`) is chosen deliberately: it is unidirectional server→browser (the browser physically cannot push), so the live feed is *read-only by construction* — the same fail-closed posture as the MCP server, enforced by the transport itself. `Last-Event-ID`/`?since=` gives resumable cursors straight onto `iter_records(since_seq=)`.\n\n3. **Live Kùzu knowledge-graph map as a second projection of the one source of truth.** `graph.query`/`entity`/`health` are already guarded and JSON-shaped. Rendered as an interactive force-directed graph (vendored local JS, no CDN). Every node carries `anchor_seq`; clicking a node opens its spine record (provenance) and pivots the timeline to that seq — the structural view and the temporal view are two windows onto the same hash-chained spine. `health().in_sync` drives a \"graph stale (rebuilt through seq N, head M)\" badge — no-fabrication honesty about lag.\n\n4. **Command palette (⌘K) that routes to KERNEL with tier-prediction.** Read queries → `sigil-kernel ask` via the existing `KernelDispatch.send` seam (status lines stripped, `[BLOCKED]`→\"needs approval\" preserved) or the read endpoints. Gated verbs → the action broker (0.2). Before running, the palette shows the **predicted WARDEN tier** by reusing the `tiers.rs` classification (exposed read-only) — so the owner sees \"this is A2, will be queued\" *before* acting. Prove-don't-guess about consequences.\n\n5. **One-tap owner-signed approve/deny with the key held safely on loopback.** The browser NEVER sees private key material. The action endpoint runs in the same trust domain as the CLI and calls `ApprovalQueue.approve/deny` (via `ensure_owner_keypair()`) exactly as `cmd_approve` does. The key stays at `KEYS_DIR/owner.priv` (0600), used only by the local process the owner started. The web button is just another front-end onto the identical signing path — the browser sends \"approve seq N\" with CSRF proof; the server signs.\n\n6. **Read-only-by-default with a CSRF-proof gated action channel (generalizing the console X-Requested-With allow-by-proof posture).** A two-plane server:\n   - **Read plane** — GET only, no write path: `/api/snapshot`, `/api/record/{seq}`, `/api/stream` (SSE), `/api/graph`, `/api/classify`. Zero side effects (MCP posture).\n   - **Action plane** — POST only, requires ALL of: bind `127.0.0.1` only; `Origin`/`Referer` == the loopback origin; a non-simple `X-SIGIL-Token` header equal to a session token minted at `sigil serve` start and **printed to the terminal** (so only someone at the machine can drive actions, and no web page can read it); `Host`-header allowlist (defeats DNS-rebinding). A3/destructive verbs require re-confirming the token (\"arm\") and a typed reason.\n\n7. **WIP-agent view + spine timeline**, both fed live by the tailer. The WIP view is a per-agent lane (reusing `snapshot`'s `recent_by_agent`/`budget_today` logic) plus the live `pending_approvals` queue. The timeline lays records on a `ts` axis, lanes by `source`, colored by `tier`/`decision`, with checkpoint (`kind==\"warden_checkpoint\"`) and consolidation markers reusing `snapshot`'s `ingest_lag` logic; each mark click-throughs to provenance.\n\n**Server tech choice:** stdlib `http.server.ThreadingHTTPServer` + a hand-rolled router, not a framework. Rationale: minimal attack surface + trivially auditable + easy `assert_no_offense()` (no heavy dependency that could transitively pull in anything), and a single-user loopback dashboard has only a handful of concurrent SSE tabs, which threads handle fine. Static assets served from `sigil/ui/static/` with a strict `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'` as defense-in-depth (the \"CSP-free\" note only means it is not the claude.ai Artifact sandbox; a real localhost app should still ship a strict CSP).\n\n### 3.2 Ordered, independently-mergeable slices\n\n| Slice | Create / modify | Exact reuse points |\n|---|---|---|\n| **WS3-0** Spine-tail primitive | create `sigil/spine/tail.py` (`SpineTailer`), create the 0.3 verify helper (e.g. `sigil/spine/verify.py`) | `SpineStore.iter_records(since_seq=)`, `.next_seq`, `reuse.digest_payload`, the chain check inside `SpineStore.verify` |\n| **WS3-1** Read-only HTTP core | create `sigil/ui/__init__.py`, `sigil/ui/server.py`, `sigil/ui/static/index.html`; modify `sigil/cli.py` (add `cmd_serve` + `sub.add_parser(\"serve\")`) | `dashboard.snapshot`, `SpineStore.get`, MCP posture from `mcp/server.py` |\n| **WS3-2** SSE live tail endpoint | modify `sigil/ui/server.py` (`/api/stream`) | `SpineTailer` (WS3-0) |\n| **WS3-3** Provenance-first front-end | create `sigil/ui/static/app.js`, `style.css` | `/api/snapshot`, `/api/record`, `/api/stream`; `snapshot` field shapes |\n| **WS3-4** Graph map endpoint + render | modify `server.py` (`/api/graph`, `/api/graph/entity`); create `sigil/ui/static/vendor/<graph-lib>` | `graph.query`/`entity`/`health` (already guarded) |\n| **WS3-5** Owner-signed action broker + CSRF-proof action plane | create `sigil/ui/actions.py` (the shared broker 0.2); modify `server.py` (`/api/action`) | `ApprovalQueue.approve/deny`, `KillSwitch.engage/release`, `PromotionPolicy.grant/revoke`, `identity.ensure_owner_keypair`, `agents.approvals.pending`/`verify_approval` — all called exactly as `cmd_approve`/`cmd_warden` do |\n| **WS3-6** Command palette → KERNEL relay | modify `server.py` (`/api/ask`, `/api/classify`); modify `app.js` (⌘K) | `voice.dispatch.KernelDispatch.send`, `tiers.rs::classify` (exposed) |\n\n### 3.3 Test + real-E2E-proof strategy per slice\n\n- **WS3-0:** deterministic doubles = `SpineStore` on a temp path. Append N records → tailer yields exactly the new ones, in order; tamper a payload → tailer flags \"integrity broken\" (does not emit as truth); truncate/rewind → detected. Real proof: run the tailer against the live `~/.sigil` spine and confirm new records appear as `sigil ingest` writes them, each with a re-verified `entry_hash`.\n- **WS3-1:** unit-test the handler with a fake store returning a canned snapshot; assert GET-only (405 on POST), binds `127.0.0.1` (assert host), `/api/record` returns `entry_hash` and 404-with-note for a missing seq (empty-not-fabrication). Real proof: `sigil serve` (background) → `curl 127.0.0.1:PORT/api/snapshot` `head_seq` == `sigil dashboard` head; fetch a record and independently re-verify its `entry_hash`.\n- **WS3-2:** connect an SSE client, append a record to the temp spine → assert it arrives with correct `seq`/`entry_hash`; assert the server ignores any client-sent body (unidirectional). Real proof: open the stream, run `sigil-kernel ask`, watch the resulting spine records stream in live.\n- **WS3-3:** keep JS thin and test the JSON contracts server-side; a small DOM-logic test for the click→`/api/record` resolver. Real proof (screenshot): click a displayed claim, see it resolve to its raw spine record + verified hash.\n- **WS3-4:** endpoint refuses a write Cypher (assert the `graph.query` error passthrough), returns columns/rows; `GraphUnavailable` → 200-with-note, no crash. Real proof: `sigil graph` then `curl /api/graph` returns real nodes whose `anchor_seq` resolves via `/api/record`.\n- **WS3-5 (security keystone):** (a) POST without token → 403; (b) cross-origin `Origin` → 403; (c) `Host: evil.com` → 403 (rebinding); (d) GET on `/api/action` → 405; (e) valid token+origin approve of a queued seq → produces a `governor.approval` record that `verify_approval` accepts against `owner_pubkey()`; (f) forged token → rejected; (g) replay the same approval onto a different seq → rejected (RP-APPROVAL-4 parity). Real proof: an agent queues an A2 → approve it in-browser → `pending(store, owner_pubkey())` no longer lists it AND the new record verifies. **Run `code-review`/red-pen AND `adversarial-sweep` on this slice specifically.**\n- **WS3-6:** `/api/ask` returns the KERNEL body; a blocked action returns \"needs approval\" (not fabricated success); `/api/classify` matches `tiers.rs` for known names. Real proof: ask a memory question in the palette, get the same answer as `sigil-kernel ask <same text>`.\n\n### 3.4 Doctrine-safety analysis + abuse vectors (WS3)\n\n- **Loopback-only:** bind `127.0.0.1` only (never `0.0.0.0`); assert the bind address in a test.\n- **Owner-signed gated actions:** no new write path — `/api/action` calls only the existing owner-signed cores; the browser never holds key material.\n- **Fail-closed:** read plane is GET-only; action plane denies on any missing proof; unknown palette verbs inherit `tiers.rs` fail-closed A3.\n- **No-fabrication:** every atom resolves to `/api/record`; empty results say so; a re-verify failure badges \"integrity broken\"; graph staleness badged.\n- **Offense-free:** `assert_no_offense()` in `ui/server.py`, `ui/actions.py`, `spine/tail.py`.\n- **Abuse vectors a reviewer will hunt:**\n  - *Malicious localhost page hitting `/api/action`* — defeated by Origin/Referer + non-simple `X-SIGIL-Token` (forces a CORS preflight that we reject cross-origin) + token secrecy (terminal-printed, never exposed to any page) + SameSite.\n  - *DNS-rebinding* (evil.com rebinds to 127.0.0.1) — defeated by the `Host`-header allowlist.\n  - *SSRF/command injection via `/api/ask`* — `KernelDispatch` shells argv (`[\"sigil-kernel\",\"ask\",text]`, no `shell=True`); text is a query, and the KERNEL's own WARDEN gate governs any action it triggers.\n  - *Cypher injection to writes* — impossible: `graph.query` refuses write keywords + uses a read-only connection + auto-LIMIT.\n  - *SSE resource exhaustion* — bounded concurrent streams, heartbeat + idle timeout, coalesced ticks.\n\n---\n\n## WORKSTREAM 4 — CROSS-PLATFORM + MOBILE BRIDGE\n\n### 4.1 Peak-innovative core mechanisms\n\n1. **Per-OS backend abstraction (`sigil/platform/`) — the first intentional platform branch in the repo.** A `HostBackend` protocol (`capture_screen`, `capture_camera`, `secret_get/set`, `audio_source/sink`, `capabilities`) with `linux.py` / `macos.py` / `windows.py` impls selected at runtime by `sys.platform`. Crucially the interface IS the current `capture.py` `Frame` contract, so the entire perception/voice stack above the seam is unchanged — this is a *pure refactor + extension*, not a rewrite. Each impl returns `None` on unavailability (the existing honest-gap posture of `capture.py`). Linux wraps the existing `scrot/tesseract/ffmpeg` + `sounddevice` code verbatim.\n\n2. **OS keyring/keychain secret store — retiring plaintext `sigil.env`.** A `SecretStore` (Keychain / Credential Manager / libsecret) resolves secrets **keyring-first, `sigil.env` fallback** (`config._load_env_file` stays as the fallback). This matters doubly because `tiers.rs` *already* classifies `secret/keyring/keychain/vault/keystore/hsm` tokens as A3 — so any agent tool that reads secrets is already destructive-explicit; `SecretStore` is owner-local plumbing that keeps secrets off the plaintext file and, critically, off the network (see §4 transport).\n\n3. **Capability-negotiation layer as SIGNED SPINE RECORDS — distributed compute, centralized authority.** Each host advertises a descriptor `{host_id, os, has_camera, has_gpu_vlm, always_on, wg_pubkey, ...}` **appended to the spine as an owner-signed `host_capability` record.** The mesh topology is therefore itself provable, tamper-evident memory — not out-of-band config. The desktop (brain, always-on) holds the source-of-truth spine; laptop/phone (limbs) sync the ONE signed spine over WireGuard. An agent needing a VLM/camera consults the latest `host_capability` records and routes work to the best-capable online host — but authorization still flows through the one spine + WARDEN gate, so a limb executes only what the brain's spine authorized. A rogue limb cannot forge \"I am the always-on desktop\" because descriptors are owner-signed against the single trust-root key. **This is \"distributed but sovereign\": compute distributed, authority centralized in the hash chain.**\n\n4. **Phone bridge = owner-signed remote approval + panic kill-switch + KERNEL relay over WireGuard**, each mapping onto an existing hardened core:\n   - **Remote approval (peak design — 1-of-N device authorization):** rather than shipping the trust-root key to the phone, extend identity to a small **owner-signed device-authorization ledger** on the spine (`device_authorized`/`device_revoked` records). The phone holds its OWN Ed25519 device key, authorized by an owner-signed spine record; approvals verify against *any currently-authorized device key* via `reuse.verify_threshold`/`verify_one` (already imported in `reuse`). This is strictly more advanced than \"borrow the desktop key\" AND lets the phone approve even when it cannot reach the desktop. `verify_approval` (approvals.py) is extended to accept the authorized-device set instead of only the single `owner_pubkey()` — preserving RP-APPROVAL-2 (trust is pinned to owner-*minted* keys, never to a key the requester merely presents) and RP-APPROVAL-4 (signed `target_seq`, no replay).\n   - **Panic kill-switch:** maps perfectly onto the *existing asymmetric* `KillSwitch` — ANY engage halts (fail-safe), so a panic-halt from the phone is honored even without a signature (worst case: a nuisance DoS-halt); a *release* still requires an owner/authorized-device signature (fail-closed). No new logic — just a transport onto `engage`/`release`.\n   - **KERNEL command relay:** phone text → desktop daemon runs `KernelDispatch.send` → same T0 router + WARDEN gate + signed action log; `[BLOCKED]`→\"needs approval.\" Voice already proved this exact path.\n\n5. **Push over the SHARED tail primitive — no cloud, no data egress.** When an A2/A3 queues, the desktop notifier — fed by the SAME `SpineTailer` (0.1) that powers the UI feed — pushes to the phone over WireGuard. Deliberately NOT Telegram/WhatsApp/cloud push: those are A2 external surfaces that would egress the private subject off owned hardware. The push carries only `{seq, tier, kind}`; the phone fetches any detail over the WireGuard-only daemon API on demand. Data never leaves the tunnel between the owner's own devices → still local-first. **One tail primitive, two consumers (UI live feed + mobile push).**\n\n### 4.2 Ordered, independently-mergeable slices\n\n| Slice | Create / modify | Exact reuse points |\n|---|---|---|\n| **WS4-0** (shared) | reuse `SpineTailer` from WS3-0 | — |\n| **WS4-1** Platform skeleton + capability probe | create `sigil/platform/__init__.py` (`host()` selector by `sys.platform`), `base.py` (`HostBackend`, `CapabilityDescriptor`), `linux.py` | move the bodies of `perception/capture.py::grab_screen/grab_camera` into `LinuxBackend`; probe via `shutil.which` (scrot/tesseract/ffmpeg) exactly as `capture.py` already does |\n| **WS4-2** Secret store | create `sigil/platform/secrets.py`; modify `sigil/config.py` (keyring-first, env fallback) | keep `config._load_env_file` as fallback |\n| **WS4-3** macOS + Windows backends | create `sigil/platform/macos.py`, `sigil/platform/windows.py` | `screencapture`/`mss`, Keychain/Credential Manager, `Frame.from_image` |\n| **WS4-4** Signed capability + device-authorization ledger | create `sigil/mesh/__init__.py`, `sigil/mesh/registry.py`; modify `sigil/agents/approvals.py` (`verify_approval` accepts the authorized-device set) | `identity.ensure_owner_keypair`, `reuse.sign`/`verify_one`/`verify_threshold`, `SpineStore.append`, `SpineStore.verify` |\n| **WS4-5** WireGuard-only desktop daemon | create `sigil/bridge/__init__.py`, `sigil/bridge/daemon.py`; modify `sigil/cli.py` (`sub.add_parser(\"bridge\")`) | the WS3-5 action broker; `agents.approvals.pending`, `KillSwitch`, `KernelDispatch.send`; WS4-4 authorized-device set |\n| **WS4-6** Phone client + push notifier | create `sigil/bridge/notifier.py` (feeds off `SpineTailer`); create the thin PWA served by the daemon under `sigil/bridge/webapp/` | `SpineTailer` (WS3-0), the daemon API (WS4-5) |\n| **WS4-7** Rust kernel + dispatch cross-OS parity | modify `kernel/src/main.rs`/`registry.rs` (2 hardcoded binary paths → `SIGIL_HOME`/PATH + `cfg(target_os)` for the OS-specific home); modify `sigil/voice/dispatch.py::_default_bin` (drop hardcoded `/home/kali/sigil` → `SIGIL_HOME`-relative) | `SIGIL_HOME` env (the existing portability lever) |\n\n### 4.3 Test + real-E2E-proof strategy per slice\n\n- **WS4-1:** monkeypatch `sys.platform` → correct backend class; monkeypatch `shutil.which` → `capabilities()` reports honest gaps (None); **regression: all existing `perception`/`voice` tests pass unchanged** (proves the refactor is behavior-preserving on Linux). Real proof: `sigil host caps` prints the real descriptor for this Kali box (screen: yes, camera: probe, GPU-VLM: probe).\n- **WS4-2:** monkeypatch keyring → `get/set` round-trips; env fallback when keyring empty; **assert no secret value is ever appended to the spine or logged** (grep the produced records).\n- **WS4-3:** on Linux CI the native tools can't run, so test the protocol contract with mocked subprocess — assert the macOS backend shells `screencapture` and the Windows backend shells the `mss`/PowerShell path (deterministic doubles). Real proof: documented manual run on a Mac/Win host (or a CI matrix if available). *This is the cross-OS-regression red-pen surface.*\n- **WS4-4 (trust-root widening — heavy red-pen):** register a device → the authorized set includes it; revoke → excluded; an *unsigned* register is ignored (fail-closed); tampering a descriptor is caught by `SpineStore.verify`; an approval signed by an authorized device verifies, one signed by an unauthorized/forged key is rejected (RP-APPROVAL-2 parity). Run `adversarial-sweep` here.\n- **WS4-5:** an approval signed by an AUTHORIZED device → accepted, produces a verifying `governor.approval`; UNAUTHORIZED/forged key → rejected; replay onto a different seq → rejected (RP-APPROVAL-4); binds only to the WireGuard interface IP (assert it refuses `0.0.0.0`/public). Real proof: two loopback network namespaces (or a real WG pair) — queue an A2 on desktop, approve from the daemon client, desktop spine shows a verifying signed approval.\n- **WS4-6:** deterministic — the notifier, given a tailer that yields a new *queued* record, emits exactly one push; NO push for A0/A1; the push payload contains only `{seq,tier,kind}` (assert no `subject`/secret). Real proof: over a real WG pair, queue an A2 → phone receives push → phone approves → desktop spine shows the verifying device-signed approval.\n- **WS4-7:** kernel resolves binary/home via env per OS (`cfg(test)` + env override); `dispatch._default_bin` finds the kernel via `SIGIL_HOME`. Real proof: run with a relocated `SIGIL_HOME` on Linux; documented Mac/Win.\n\n### 4.4 Doctrine-safety analysis + abuse vectors (WS4)\n\n- **Loopback-only / owned-hardware-only:** the daemon binds the WireGuard interface IP only (owner's own devices, encrypted tunnel) — never `0.0.0.0`/public; assert in test. Push stays inside the tunnel; no cloud push.\n- **Owner-signed gated actions:** approvals verify against the owner-*minted* authorized-device set (`verify_threshold`); device authorization/revocation are themselves owner-signed spine records. No unsigned remote write path.\n- **Fail-closed:** killswitch engage fail-safe / release fail-closed (unchanged); missing owner key → None → nothing trusted; unauthorized device → rejected; capability probe returns None rather than fabricating a capture.\n- **No-fabrication:** capability descriptors are provable spine records; a limb's advertised capability is auditable; the mesh routes on cited records, not on unverified claims.\n- **Offense-free:** `assert_no_offense()` in `platform/*`, `mesh/registry.py`, `bridge/daemon.py`, `bridge/notifier.py`.\n- **Abuse vectors a reviewer will hunt:**\n  - *Forged remote approval* — verified against the current authorized-device set (RP-APPROVAL-2 pin); replay onto another seq rejected (signed `target_seq`, RP-APPROVAL-4); a rogue device cannot self-authorize (authorization is owner-signed).\n  - *Secret leakage in transport* — secrets live in the OS keyring, never on the spine, never in a push payload; WireGuard encrypts the tunnel; no off-device egress. Assert no secret in logs/records/pushes.\n  - *Cross-OS regressions* — Linux path is a behavior-preserving refactor (existing tests unchanged); macOS/Windows are additive; honest-gap `None` everywhere.\n  - *Malicious host joining the mesh* — a capability descriptor from an un-authorized device is ignored; only owner-signed descriptors count toward routing/authority.\n  - *Panic-halt abuse* — engage is intentionally unauthenticated-honored (fail-safe); the only asymmetric risk (nuisance halt) is by design the safe direction.\n\n---\n\n## 5. Recommended sequencing + shared primitives\n\n**Build order (dependency- and risk-ordered):**\n\n1. **WS3-0 spine-tail primitive + verify helper** — small, pure, high-leverage; powers both the UI feed and mobile push. Build and red-pen it in isolation first.\n2. **WS3-1 → WS3-3 read-only cockpit** — fastest value, smallest attack surface (a loopback GET server), and it exercises the tailer end-to-end in the safest context before any write path exists.\n3. **WS3-5 action broker (owner-signed, CSRF-proof)** — the security keystone and a *shared primitive*. Build, red-pen, and `adversarial-sweep` it in the LOCAL loopback context **before any remote surface exists**. WS3-4/3-6 can slot in around it.\n4. **WS4-1 → WS4-3 platform abstraction + secrets** — can run **in parallel** with all of WS3 (disjoint files: `sigil/platform/*` vs `sigil/ui/*`). Land before the mobile daemon so a macOS/Windows machine can host the daemon.\n5. **WS4-4 device-authorization ledger** — trust-root widening; must land + be red-penned/adversarial-swept **before any remote signer exists**.\n6. **WS4-5 → WS4-6 mobile bridge** — LAST, because it composes all three shared primitives (tailer + action broker + device ledger) and is the highest-risk surface (remote + auth + trust-widening).\n7. **WS4-7 kernel/dispatch cross-OS parity** — independent, do it anytime.\n\n**Shared primitives (built once, consumed twice):**\n\n- **`SpineTailer` (WS3-0)** → UI SSE live feed **and** mobile push notifier.\n- **Owner-signed action broker (WS3-5 `ui/actions.py`)** → UI action plane **and** mobile daemon; owner-key handling + Origin/token/Host proof + tier prediction written once.\n- **Capability/identity chain** → the platform probe (WS4-1) feeds the signed `host_capability` records (WS4-4); the UI is the degenerate single-host view that renders the mesh.\n- **`verify_record` helper (0.3)** → UI `/api/record`, the tailer, and the daemon all prove-don't-guess through one implementation.\n\nEach workstream closes on the historical cadence: **deterministic tests (temp-`SpineStore`, `StaticFrame`, `FileAudioSource/FileSink`, `generate_keypair` doubles, monkeypatched `sys.platform`/`shutil.which`, twin loopback namespaces) + a real end-to-end proof + red-pen + `adversarial-sweep` (especially on WS3-5 and WS4-4/4-5) + fixes before merge.**\n\n---\n\n### Critical Files for Implementation\n- /home/kali/sigil/sigil/spine/store.py — the poll-only cursor (`iter_records(since_seq=)`, `next_seq`, `verify`) that the shared `SpineTailer` and the `/api/record` provenance endpoint are built on.\n- /home/kali/sigil/sigil/dashboard.py — `snapshot(store)->dict` is the entire cockpit JSON contract; the UI renders exactly this dict.\n- /home/kali/sigil/sigil/agents/approvals.py — the RP-hardened owner-signed approval core (`ApprovalQueue`, `pending`, `verify_approval`) that both the in-browser one-tap approve and the remote phone approval reuse and extend (device-set verification).\n- /home/kali/sigil/sigil/mcp/server.py — the reference read-only / fail-closed / provenance-on-every-result network-surface posture to mirror in `sigil/ui/server.py`.\n- /home/kali/sigil/sigil/perception/capture.py — the `Frame`/`StaticFrame` contract and honest-gap `None` posture that becomes the `HostBackend` interface in the new `sigil/platform/` package.\n\nSupporting reuse anchors: /home/kali/sigil/sigil/governor/identity.py + /home/kali/sigil/sigil/governor/killswitch.py (owner-key holders), /home/kali/sigil/sigil/voice/dispatch.py (`KernelDispatch` KERNEL relay), /home/kali/sigil/kernel/src/tiers.rs (tier prediction), /home/kali/sigil/sigil/config.py (`SIGIL_HOME` portability lever + secret-store seam),
